capabilities.title: Local React application with loopback service and typed client
capabilities.contract: The renderer uses a typed application client against the local Node.js service; credentials and privileged operations remain server-side.
capabilities.persistence: No renderer access to secrets, files, or SQLite.

capabilities.title: Health reporting and recoverable client errors
capabilities.contract: Health and stable error codes allow the renderer to present recoverable failures without exposing secrets or full Article bodies.
capabilities.persistence: Errors are transient UI state; sensitive values are not included in the transport contract.

capabilities.title: Separate Editorial Workspace and Application Settings screens
capabilities.contract: Application Settings is a workspace-level screen and never belongs to Article Revision history.
capabilities.persistence: Screen selection is renderer state; Application Settings persist through their dedicated service contracts.

capabilities.title: Single-user, local-first operation
capabilities.contract: Articles, Draft checkpoints, materials, style samples, and settings persist in local SQLite storage through domain-specific repositories wired at local-service startup.
capabilities.persistence: SQLite is the active data store; private author data is not delegated to a remote application database.

capabilities.title: Desktop-ready responsive shell
capabilities.contract: The desktop shell supports collapsed panels and responsive workspace layout.
capabilities.persistence: Workspace layout preferences are persisted locally in browser storage.
limitations: Electron, mobile, and offline modes remain deferred.

scenarios.title: Typed client translates service conflicts safely
preconditions: The local service responds with a Draft conflict.
scenarios.event: The renderer saves a Draft through HttpApplicationClient.
expected: The client throws the typed renderer-safe conflict error.
forbidden: The renderer does not receive server internals or credentials.

scenarios.title: Client-visible failures use stable error codes
preconditions: An Assistant request fails before or during streaming.
scenarios.event: The application client receives the service response.
expected: The client exposes a stable error code for recoverable UI handling.
forbidden: Raw provider details are not rendered as the user-facing failure.

scenarios.title: Opening Settings preserves the workspace context
preconditions: An Article is open in the Editorial Workspace.
expected: Application Settings is displayed without creating an empty Article workspace.
forbidden: Opening Settings does not alter Article Revision history.

scenarios.title: Local data survives reopening SQLite
preconditions: An Article, Draft checkpoint, material, setting, artifact, and citation exist.
scenarios.event: The SQLite database is closed and reopened.
expected: The persisted local data can be read after reopening.
forbidden: Persistence does not require a remote application database.

scenarios.title: Desktop shell restores panel layout preferences
preconditions: Stored workspace layout settings are present.
expected: The desktop shell restores its panel layout and clears migrated legacy keys.
forbidden: A missing preference does not prevent the workspace from rendering.
